The **2023 Zürich cantonal elections** were held on 12 February 2023[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:2-2) to elect the seven members of the cantonal [Executive Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Council_of_Z%C3%BCrich "Executive Council of Zürich") and the 180 members of the [Cantonal Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonal_Council_of_Z%C3%BCrich "Cantonal Council of Zürich").
All seven incumbents in the Executive Council were re-elected, with the bourgeois alliance holding a majority of four; in the Cantonal Council the "Climate alliance" retained a narrow majority of 91.
## Electoral system
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Electoral system")]
### Executive Council
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Executive Council")]
The Executive Council contains 7 members elected using a two-round majoritarian system. In the first round, electors have up to seven votes and the 7 most-popular candidates reaching an overall majority (>50%) are elected. If 7 candidates do not reach majority and seats remain to be filled, a runoff election is held where electors have as many votes as seats remaining ([plurality block voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plurality_block_voting "Plurality block voting")). The candidates with the most votes (simple plurality) are elected to fill the open seats.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:5-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:6-4)
### Cantonal Council
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Cantonal Council")]
The Cantonal Council is elected using open-list proportional representation, with canton-wide apportionment of seats and allocation into 18 constituencies ([biproportional apportionment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biproportional_apportionment "Biproportional apportionment"), with seat count per district pre-set before the election). 
In each constituency, voters have as many votes as there are seats to fill ([panachage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panachage "Panachage") is permitted); these votes each count both for the candidate and for the list they stand in. These votes counts are divided by the seat count to give _fictional electors_ counts which can be summed up fairly throughout the canton.
Using the fictional electors counts, each party above the threshold (reaching 5% in at least one constituency) is apportioned seats canton-wide, which are then shared among their constituency lists. In each constituency list, the seats are attributed to the candidates reaching the most votes.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:5-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:6-4)

### Date
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Date")]
Cantonal elections in Zürich are typically held in April or late March, but the presence of both a federal referendum date on 12 March and holidays meant the cantonal elections had to be pusher earlier, to mid-February.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:3-5) Had a second round been needed, it would have been held on 16 April.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:3-5)
## Candidates
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Candidates")]
### Executive Council
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Executive Council")]
All seven incumbents ran for re-election: Mario Fehr (ind.), Jacqueline Fehr (SP), [Ernst Stocker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_Stocker_\(politician\)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ernst Stocker \(politician\) \(page does not exist\)") (SVP), Sylvia Steiner (CVP), Carmen Walker Späh (FDP), Martin Neukom (Grüne), and Natalie Rickli (SVP). Mario Fehr was elected in 2011 then re-elected in 2015 and 2019 as a social democrat, but left the party in 2021 and contested this election as an independent.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:3-5)
The FDP fielded Peter Grünenfelder as their second candidate in hope of retaking their seat lost in 2015; the SP fielded Priska Seiler Graf as their second candidate to compensate for Mario Fehr's defection. Benno Scherrer runs for the Green-Liberals, hoping to take a seat as the fourth-largest party in the cantonal council.
Minor candidates were Anne-Claude Hensch for the Alternative List, Daniel Sommer for the EVP; Patrick Jetzer for Aufrecht and Josua Dietrich for the Free List both ran as opponents to Covid restrictions. Former SVP member Hans-Peter Amrein also ran as an independent, as did Bernhard Schmidt and Peter Vetsch.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:3-5)
Candidacies could be submitted until 28 November 2022, 17 candidates ran in total.

The [2019 cantonal elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections "2019 Zürich cantonal elections") had been a “green wave” as both the GLP and Greens gained over five percentage points in the Cantonal Council. The parties of the loose "Climate Alliance" (SP, GLP, Greens, EVP, AL) had won an overall majority for the first time, with 94 seats (out of 180).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:3-5) The BDP, which failed to pass the threshold in 2019, merged with the CVP to form Die Mitte (The Centre).
As in previous elections, the bourgeois parties (SVP, FDP, Mitte) ran running as an alliance for the executive council.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-9) The SP, Greens, and AL also recommend each-other's candidates under the name “Progressive Alliance”.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-10) Both were more cohesive alliances than in previous elections;[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:4-11) the GLP and other parties were in no alliance for the Executive Council.
Education policy was an important issue in the campaign; although surveys saw climate and the environment as the most important issue, followed by immigration and asylum, pensions and social security, and health care. An explanation is electoral strategy, since the lowest-polling incumbent, Sylvia Steiner, was leading the education department. New candidates Priska Seiler Graf, Peter Grünenfelder, and Benno Scherrer have criticized her education policy.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:4-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-13)

This election saw little movement for most parties. The most significant changes were the Green Party losing three seats, while The Centre (merger of the CVP and BDP) re-gained three, mainly owing to the inclusion of former BDP votes that failed to pass the threshold in 2019. The SVP retained the first place and gained one seat, as did the Social-Democrats and the Green-Liberals; the EVP, AL, and EDU all lost one seat each, and the FDP's number of seats remained consistent. No new party passed the threshold, Aufrecht and the Free List came closest but did not win any seats.
The "Climate Alliance" (SP, GLP, Greens, EVP, AL) lost three seats overall but maintained a narrow majority of a single seat, while the bourgeois parties (SVP, FDP, CVP) gained four seats but failed to re-gain the majority. This puts once again the Green-Liberals as kingmakers for various legislative majorities in the elected Cantonal Council, left-leaning for social and climate issues but right-leaning for economic issues.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Z%C3%BCrich_cantonal_elections#cite_note-:1-19)
